reason: The cited lines say the tool evaluates an arbitrary JavaScript function in a target browser page or service worker and returns the result as JSON. That is browser/page-context execution, not arbitrary host execution, so HOSTEXEC is not supported. Because page-context JavaScript can read page DOM/data such as title or innerText and use the page/session context, returning that result can expose non-public page/SaaS data to the agent, supporting SECRET. The example includes `fetch("example.com")`, showing the evaluated script can make requests to agent-chosen web destinations, supporting SINK. Returned values can also come from the target page or fetched web content, which may be attacker-controlled, supporting UNTRUSTED.
